text: The Iberian electricity market split on 2026-08-18 from 07:45Z to 15:15Z, with Portugal pricing 109.84 EUR/MWh above Spain at the worst interval (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). At 10:15Z, the peak of the episode, Portugal reached 110.73 EUR/MWh while Spain fell to 0.89 EUR/MWh, with the border between them fully saturated at 3,330 MW flowing from Spain to Portugal against available capacity of 3,330 MW (ENTSO-E A44 and A09). The full border and price separation are consistent with each other but both reflect the market coupling's response to underlying constraints; the published notices do not establish direct causation between the two. A planned outage on the Alcochete-Palmela transmission asset reduced its availability to 2,800 MW (ENTSO-E A78, with 12 notices in force from publication on 2026-07-23), and while A78 asset-level data and A61 border capacity are related, they measure different quantities after the operator's security assessment, so the difference between them is not an error. The price separation cost importers into Portugal an extra 1,853,272.39 EUR over the 7.5-hour episode (ENTSO-E A44 with A09 scheduled flows).

The Iberian electricity market split on 2026-08-19 from 07:30Z to 15:00Z, with Portugal trading at a severe premium of 108.16 EUR/MWh above Spain (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). The Spain-Portugal border operated at full capacity throughout the episode: the net flow from Spain to Portugal matched the available capacity of 3,333 MW at the peak interval, and all 30 settlement intervals showed saturated conditions (ENTSO-E A09 scheduled exchanges and A61 day-ahead capacity). The Alcochete-Palmela transmission asset was unavailable due to planned maintenance, with 2,800 MW out of service under 12 active notices published from 2026-07-23 (ENTSO-E A78 transmission unavailability). The border saturation and price separation are consistent with the constrained transmission, though the A78 asset-level unavailability of 2,800 MW and the A61 net border capacity of 3,333 MW represent different measurements reflecting the operator's security assessment, and the published notices do not explicitly state that the maintenance caused the market split.
